gaps: The recorded worker boundary was broader than the approved remaining-work boundary.
The task promised a board migration without reconciling the existing board reader or write scope.
`forge task close` ownership and the stale-stamp/sequential behavior were unresolved.
The new evidence contract lacked an exact generation, selection, origin, and recorder interface.
The meaning and representation of raw helper bytes were undefined.
The lens tag and finding fingerprint could not be derived from the installed helper schema.
Quality verdict extraction was not isolated to validated quality assessment blocks.
Publication had incompatible rules for failure before and after pointer replacement.
Rejection could race a concurrent selection and overwrite an unselected source.
The required tests did not falsify eight mandatory generation, upgrade, routing, and consumer invariants.
The filesystem topology rule incorrectly treated ancestor directories like regular single-link files.
`reviewer_focus` restated load-bearing rules without citing the constitution.
The helper identity and SHA could describe different bytes from the executable actually launched.
resolutions: The final decomposition records the complete accumulated task as 75 paths and 58 tests, while the approved task plan limits the remaining delegate to exactly 16 existing paths plus one new schema and 2,500 changed lines. Every other in-envelope path is preserve-byte-for-byte input, and any additional path or line overrun stops for amendment.

The existing board task-progress path already calls `task_proof_problems`, so it will consume the shared selected-generation predicate without editing `board.py`. Its separate fixed-file story summary remains non-authoritative display and belongs to the later Shared journey.

The scope now includes `factory/scripts/forge_cli/close.py`. `stamp_is_fresh` becomes the shared selected-clean/current-delta predicate used by closeout and stage consumers, and `forge.py`, `close.py`, and `review.py` remove the obsolete sequential CLI, environment, and internal plumbing.

The task plan now enumerates exact generation, helper, input, raw-result, lens, rejection, upgrade, and selection fields. It defines `record_review_from_json.py --set --task <id> --input <candidate.json>` as the complete-set interface, mutually exclusive with diagnostic `--aspect`, with one shared schema-backed publication function for review, rejection, and upgrade.

The generation stores `raw_result={encoding: base64, sha256, bytes, data}` where `data` is RFC 4648 base64 of the exact bytes read once from the helper JSON-output file before UTF-8 JSON parsing. Rejection preserves that exact decoded byte sequence and metadata.

Finding titles begin with exactly one `[quality] `, `[performance] `, or `[security] ` token. The helper supplies one integer line, so start and end both equal it; duplicate identity is NFC POSIX repository-relative path, the integer start/end pair, and NFC whitespace-collapsed case-folded title after removing the tag, with no category component.

Only `VERDICT` lines inside each actual pass's validated quality assessment block count. Performance and security blocks, finding bodies, and the synthesized chunk summary cannot supply or worsen a quality verdict.

Pointer replacement is now the publication commit point. Failure before replacement preserves the prior pointer byte-for-byte; a later stage-stamp failure keeps the new pointer selected, and retry validates and stamps that same current generation.

The existing cross-platform protected task lock gains kind `review-selection` and covers source read, source validation, generation publication, final selected-source comparison, pointer replacement, and stamping. A rejection refuses if selection changed after its source read.

The decomposition adds eight named invariant cases, raising the task to 58 required tests and the focused batch to nineteen selectors. They cover generation-ID tampering, idempotent retry and collision, exact sealed upgrade binding, rejection CAS, board selection, close/frontier current-delta routing, origin/raw-byte validation, and helper identity mismatch.

Every existing ancestor of a generation, selection, or same-directory temporary path must be a real non-symlink directory. Existing and new leaves must be regular single-link files; exclusive no-follow temporary creation, hard-link/no-overwrite generation publication, and atomic pointer replacement have separate explicit rules.

The final `reviewer_focus` cites `constitution/README.md` and its conduct sections directly, while the task plan invokes ponytail's minimum-diff ladder and the exact preserve/stop boundary instead of re-deriving the repository law.

The runner resolves one real regular helper path, captures version, file identity, and SHA immediately before launch, then re-resolves and rechecks the same identity after exit and before publication. Any mismatch discards the attempt without pointer or stamp mutation.
